  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>On that day, the writing of the Torah scroll began in secret, as announced by the special committee.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And indeed, on that day the writing of the Torah scroll began in secret,</t>
    <t s="1">as stated in a special announcement,</t>
    <t s="2">on behalf of the "Torah Scroll Committee for Welcoming Moshiach"5,</t>
    <t s="3">in "Hakriah Vehakedushah"6</t>
    <t s="4">: it took place according to the Rebbe's</t>
    <t s="5">(shlita)</t>
    <t s="6">[n"a]</t>
    <t s="7">wish without publicity7.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Torah scroll was written on special parchment from slaughtered and kosher hides, and the Rebbe Rayatz requested it be processed in the Holy Land.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">The writing of the Torah scroll was on special parchment of slaughtered and kosher hides8.</t>
    <t s="1">And furthermore, the Rebbe, the Admor Moharayatz n"a, wanted the parchment to be processed in the Holy Land,</t>
    <t s="2">and he turned with this request via telegram to Moreinu Harav Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov9.</t>
    <t s="3">And in a more detailed letter to him,</t>
    <t s="4">on 2 Menachem Av10.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Rebbe Rayatz sent a telegram requesting kosher parchment of six handbreadths to write a Torah scroll to welcome Moshiach.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"I sent a telegram to my friend shiy" regarding obtaining parchment from slaughtered and kosher hides processed for its sake—in the measure of six handbreadths—for writing, with G-d's help, a Torah scroll with which to welcome Moshiach Tzidkeinu very soon."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
